title: Anticipated experienced and remembered subjective effort and discomfort
key_finding: Sustained attention produced more effort than anticipated; effort and discomfort dissociate temporally

title: Mental effort and discomfort: peak-end effect
key_finding: Discomfort increased over task duration while effort decreased; peak-end effect applies to cognitive discomfort

title: Dissociation between mental fatigue and motivational state
key_finding: Mental fatigue and motivation dissociate during prolonged cognitive work; fatigue increases while motivation fluctuates

title: Engagement of mental effort in response to mental fatigue
key_finding: 49% of participants showed effort disengagement; distinct psychophysiological profiles for engagement vs disengagement

title: Effects of mental fatigue on effort allocation
key_finding: Mental fatigue alters effort allocation via reward/cost trade-off mechanism

title: Fatigue and Human Performance: Updated Framework
key_finding: Updated framework: fatigue reflects effort costs including intrinsic and opportunity costs; younger adults perceive tasks as more effortful

title: Mental Fatigue Negatively Impacts Performance
key_finding: Large-scale confirmation: 45-min cognitive load impairs subsequent cognitive and physical performance

title: Computational mechanisms of physical and cognitive fatigue
key_finding: Fatigue fluctuates trial-by-trial as function of exerted effort; errors specifically induce cognitive fatigue; computational model of fatigue dynamics

title: Cognitive fatigue: Time-based Resource-sharing
key_finding: Processing time-related cognitive load leads to subjective cognitive fatigue and decreased alertness

title: What Is Mental Effort: A Clinical Perspective
effort_measure: Effort as cognitive work vs subjective experience
key_finding: Two meanings of mental effort conflated: cognitive work done vs subjective experience; distinction critical for understanding fatigue

title: Neuro-metabolic account of daylong cognitive work
key_finding: Glutamate accumulates in lPFC during sustained cognitive work; drives shift toward low-effort economic choices; neuro-metabolic theory of fatigue

title: Considerations on gradual glutamate accumulation
key_finding: Critically evaluates glutamate accumulation hypothesis; MRS captures total glutamate not just extracellular; replication needed

title: Potential role of glutamate transport in mental fatigue
key_finding: Foundational proposal: decreased glutamate transmission as cellular correlate of mental fatigue; extracellular glutamate inhibits LC and raphe nuclei

title: Glutamate increase in mPFC during mental imagery
key_finding: Glx concentration increases in mPFC during cognitive task vs rest; extends sensory cortex findings to higher-order regions

title: MRS glutamate in exhaustion syndrome
key_finding: Glutamate elevated in ACC/mPFC in exhaustion patients; linearly correlated with perceived stress level

title: Cognitive cost as dynamic energetic allocation
key_finding: Astrocytic glycogen as energetic buffer; brain rationally conserves activity to manage energy budget; connects to hypoglycemia effects

title: Neural integration of risk effort and time
key_finding: Left-lateralized network (anterior insula, ACC, striatum) tracks both task demand and fatigue-state; fatigue x load interaction in effort ratings

title: Active interoceptive inference and emotional brain
key_finding: Bodily states actively predicted; errors generate aversive feelings including discomfort; pain = failed suppression of interoceptive prediction error

title: Active inference theory of allostasis in depression
key_finding: Depression/fatigue as disorder of allostasis; locked-in brain insensitive to sensory context; energy regulation at core

title: Interoceptive inference emotion embodied self
discomfort_measure: Subjective feeling states from interoceptive inference
key_finding: Emotions arise from actively-inferred generative models of interoceptive afferents; generalizes appraisal theories

title: Interoceptive predictions in the brain
key_finding: EPIC model: agranular visceromotor cortices issue interoceptive predictions; disrupted predictions = vulnerability for illness

title: Simulating interoceptive control via active inference
key_finding: Formal model: homeostatic allostatic and goal-directed interoceptive control all minimize prediction error

title: Computational Models of Interoception
key_finding: Review of computational interoception frameworks; extends classical homeostatic control to include flexible adaptive behavior

title: Self-control linked to interoceptive inference
key_finding: Self-control failures occur when predicted interoceptive models are inaccurate; links cognitive control to interoceptive inference

title: Allostatic Self-efficacy fatigue depression
discomfort_measure: Fatigue as allostatic signal, metacognitive theory
key_finding: Fatigue = metacognitive signal of dyshomeostasis; driven by divergence between expected and actual interoceptive states

title: Opportunity cost model of subjective effort
key_finding: Effort feels aversive because engaging in one task forecloses other activities; fatigue is motivating signal not exhaustion

title: Effort paradox: costly and valued
key_finding: Effort is both costly (aversive) and valued (retrospective); tension between prospective discounting and retrospective valuation

title: Expected value of control: ACC function
key_finding: dACC computes expected value of control integrating payoff amount of control and effort cost; signals when cost exceeds benefit

title: Rational Mechanistic Account of Mental Effort
key_finding: Comprehensive mechanistic account: effort allocation reflects rational cost-benefit computation; dACC as key arbitrator

title: dACC and the value of control
key_finding: dACC specifies optimal control allocation by determining EVC; licenses associated cognitive effort

title: Aversive motivation and cognitive control
key_finding: Aversive motivation modulates cognitive control via dACC-dopamine-serotonin interactions; extends EVC to mixed-incentive contexts

title: Motivational Effects of Cognitive Fatigue
key_finding: Cognitive fatigue increased effort discounting; participants chose lower-effort options after sustained cognitive work

title: Neurobiology of Cognitive Fatigue and Effort-Based Choice
key_finding: Cognitive fatigue decreases willingness to exert effort; dlPFC exertion signals functionally coupled with rIns at choice time

title: Intrinsic cost of cognitive control
key_finding: Cognitive control carries intrinsic subjective costs beyond opportunity costs; should be investigated like other economic costs

title: Cognitive effort: neuroeconomic approach
key_finding: Neuroeconomic framework: cognitive effort as cost in decision-making; ACC-striatum circuit tracks effort costs

title: Decision making and avoidance of cognitive demand
key_finding: People systematically avoid cognitive demand when given choice; first behavioral economic demonstration of cognitive effort aversion

title: Fatigue effects in cognitive pupillometry
key_finding: Task-evoked pupil response diminishes 60%+ over experiment; social interaction breaks partially restore; fatigue is unavoidable artifact

title: Pupil dilation as effort index
key_finding: Pupil dilation tracks cognitive effort across updating switching inhibition; effort account explains diverging dilation-performance patterns

title: Central mechanisms of stress-induced headache
key_finding: Headache in 91% of TTH vs 4% of healthy controls during cognitive stress; stress triggers headache via hyperalgesia on existing sensitivity
